transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2025-11-17
Time: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~55 mins
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood CSM), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Nina Alvarez (Arcadia Head of Platform), Eric Zhao (Arcadia SRE), Priya Menon (Arcadia Security), Jason Cole (Arcadia CTO)

Auto Summary (auto-generated, may be partial):
Redwood walked Arcadia through activation plan for private/VPC deployment, network requirements, and security artifacts. Main asks: VPC peering vs VPC endpoint options, CIDR/firewall requirements, SOC2 docs, and a follow-up sizing workshop for dedicated capacity. Action items and timeline agreed.

Topics Covered:
- VPC networking and peering options
- Data residency and encryption (KMS/HSM)
- Dedicated capacity sizing and autoscale patterns
- Onboarding checklist and trial tenant walkthrough
- Security docs and compliance questions

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood CSM): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We wanted to run through the activation plan and the VPC/wiring details so your infra team has everything they need. How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Nina (Arcadia): Good, thanks Maya. We had a quick internal sync, trying to confirm what we need from Redwood vs what we handle on our side.
[00:20] Liam (Redwood SE): Hi all, Liam here. I can take the tech bits — networking, peering, perf benchmarks. Quick note: apologies in advance if I say "Redwood Private" weirdly, my voice is a little fuzzy today.
[00:33] Eric (Arcadia SRE): No worries. Our main question up front is around VPC connectivity: peering vs private endpoint. We run a fairly locked-down network with a centralized proxy and strict egress controls.
[00:45] Liam: Totally. For that pattern we usually recommend VPC endpoint + PrivateLink in front of Redwood's ingestion layer, because peering can be hairy with overlapping CIDRs. But if you prefer peering we can support that too, we just need clear CIDR maps and routing.
[00:59] Priya (Security): When you say PrivateLink, what about cross-account access and audit logs? We need to ensure we can pull request logs into Splunk and have KMS control for any persisted artifacts.
[01:12] Liam: Good question. For PrivateLink we expose interface endpoints under your account boundary; logs are emitted to our control plane but we can push syslog/CloudWatch exports. Regarding KMS, if you go with Private (on-prem/VPC) option we have KMS integration — you can provide a CMK for data at rest. For hosted we encrypt with our KMS but provide certificate and key rotation docs.
[01:36] Maya: To add, we'll share the SOC2 and encryption whitepaper after this call. I'll include docs about RBAC and audit log retention too.
[01:45] Jason (CTO): That'd be great. Also want to validate latency expectations — our SLA for customer-facing features is 250ms p95. Can Redwood hit that with the quantized models we're evaluating?
[01:58] Liam: Short answer: depends on model size and sequence length. For smaller embed/generation models and with KV cache + batching tuned, hitting sub-250ms p95 for simple prompts is feasible on dedicated capacity. We'll need to run sample traces to give a definitive number; that's what the perf workshop is for.
[02:18] Eric: OK, perf workshop — what do you need from us to run that?
[02:24] Liam: We'll need example prompt traces, typical token lengths, concurrency targets, and a sample workload or a small test harness. I can send a template for request traces.
[02:33] Nina: We'll pull traces from our staging logs. Any constraints on scrubbed data? We can't share real PII.
[02:39] Liam: Totally understood. Scrubbed traces are fine — we only need the timing and token distribution. If you want, we can provide a synthetic generator that mirrors your distribution.
[02:51] Priya: Regarding compliance: you mentioned SOC2 earlier. We run rotating keys via our HSM and require mutual TLS for service endpoints. Does Redwood support mTLS + customer-managed keys?
[03:05] Maya: Yes — for Private we support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations and can enable mTLS between your VPC and our gateway. There's a bit of setup for cert provisioning, but we have a playbook for that. We'll share the cert rotation steps.
[03:22] Jason: I also want to confirm whether audit logs contain prompt text or are token counts only. From a privacy point we need no raw prompts persisted in logs.
[03:31] Liam: By default we keep request metadata and rolling token stats, not full prompt storage. But if you elect to retain full transcripts for fine-tuning or eval pipelines, that's an opt-in and subject to a separate storage policy. We'll document default retention policies in the security pack.
[03:50] Eric: Great. Networking specifics: our infra team uses 10.64.0.0/16 internally, and we already have a few peered accounts. If we need to avoid overlap, how flexible is Redwood on CIDR selection for endpoints?
[04:04] Liam: We can provision interface endpoints in your VPC space; they don't require unique global CIDR, but peering requires no overlap. For peering route tables we'll need the exact CIDR blocks you want reachable. I'll flag this as an action item.
[04:19] Nina: Perfect. On the onboarding checklist, what's the typical time to go from trial tenant to production?
[04:26] Maya: For mid-market like you, with a Private VPC setup and dedicated capacity sizing, expect ~4-8 weeks from kickoff: initial network setup and certs (1-2w), perf benchmarking and tuning (1-2w), integration tests and rollout plan (2-4w). We can tighten if you want to prioritize minimal viable paths.
[04:44] Jason: We probably want a minimal path to start pushing features — get a hosted trial in place while we prep VPC. Can you provision a trial tenant?
[04:50] Maya: Yes, we'll provision a trial tenant and give you demo credentials. Liam will also include the test harness.
[04:58] Liam: I'll spin up a small sandbox on our dedicated staging cluster and send instructions for the harness.
[05:05] Priya: A couple of specific security questions from our team: 1) Do you support SCIM for provisioning? 2) Are there hard guarantees about data deletion on contract termination?
[05:16] Maya: SCIM yes — we support SAML/SCIM for provisioning and RBAC. Data deletion: we have documented procedures and deletion certificates. We'll provide the SLA and deletion process in writing.
[05:27] Eric: On the perf side, curious about batching and KV cache — if we have high concurrency during peak hours, what failure modes should we expect? e.g., token throttling or increased latency?
[05:40] Liam: With workload-aware batching we can maintain throughput but peak latency might rise if the batch waits to fill; we have policies to prioritize low-latency requests. KV cache helps reduce compute for repeated contexts. In our Dedicated offering we can configure a latency-first policy that reduces batching windows at the cost of compute efficiency.
[05:58] Nina: Is autoscaling instant? We have sudden bursts and need predictable capacity.
[06:04] Liam: Autoscaling has a warm-up — for GPU-backed capacity there's a provisioning lead time. We support reserved burst capacity and prewarmed nodes for critical flows. For strict SLOs we recommend a minimal reserved capacity plus small autoscale headroom.
[06:20] Jason: Okay that hits our needs. Let's talk dates: can we do a sizing workshop next week?
[06:26] Maya: Week of 11/24 is open on our side. Liam, you ok to lead the workshop?
[06:31] Liam: Yep, I'll lead. I propose a 90-minute session: perf goals, sample traces, expected concurrency, and model variant recommendations.
[06:40] Priya: We'll also need a security deep dive with your security engineer — is that separate?
[06:45] Maya: Yes, we'll set up a 45-minute security review with one of our security leads. I'll include that in the follow-up invite.
[06:53] Eric: For logging integration, is there a way to push audit logs into our Splunk via forwarder?
[06:59] Liam: We can export logs via syslog/HTTP to your Splunk endpoint. We'll need the ingestion endpoint and credentials; native forwarder config can be shared.
[07:08] Nina: Anything else from the Redwood side?
[07:12] Maya: I'll enumerate all artifacts in an email: VPC guide, Private deploy playbook, SOC2 docs, RBAC and SCIM guides, and the perf workshop invite.
[07:21] Jason: Sounds good. Quick clarifying Q: Bursting — does it incur additional per-token cost while bursting?
[07:28] Liam: Yes, burst capacity has a different cost profile; we'll include cost estimates in the sizing workshop and give you tradeoffs (latency vs cost) for each policy.
[07:36] Priya: We also want to confirm data residency — some customers require EU-only. We're US-based but have EU customers; will that matter?
[07:45] Maya: Redwood supports region pinning for model serving. If you need EU-only storage/serving we'll architect the deployment accordingly; that'll factor into the Dedicated or Private deployment decisions.
[07:58] Eric: OK, last technical ask: do you have a standard set of health endpoints and SLO alerts we can subscribe to?
[08:06] Liam: Yes, we expose healthcheck endpoints and Prometheus metrics for latency, token rates, error rates. We can also give you Grafana dashboards or integrate with your monitoring stack.
[08:18] Nina: Excellent. Should we walk through the onboarding doc now?
[08:22] Maya: Quick run-through: Step 1 - NDA/contract cadence (if needed). Step 2 - Network prep: send CIDR, firewall rules, certs. Step 3 - Trial tenant prov. Step 4 - Perf workshop. Step 5 - Security deep dive. Step 6 - Staging integration and smoke tests. Step 7 - Go-live and runbooks.
[08:44] Jason: That's fine. We should be able to get CIDR + firewall info to you by Wednesday.
[08:49] Eric: We'll also share sanitized traces by Friday.
[08:53] Maya: Perfect. I'll send the VPC template and the test harness. Liam, anything to add?
[08:58] Liam: I'll attach a short checklist for the perf inputs and a link to the sandbox API key. Also I'll note one gotcha: if you use a shared proxy with header stripping, you'll need to allow the X-Request-Id header for tracing.
[09:12] Priya: Good to know.
[09:15] Maya: Alright, quick recap and next steps: 1) Maya sends VPC guide, SOC2 docs, and onboarding checklist (action). 2) Liam will draft perf plan and provision sandbox. 3) Arcadia to send CIDR + firewall + scrubbed traces. 4) Schedule sizing workshop week of 11/24 and security deep dive the following week.
[09:38] Jason: Works for me.
[09:40] Nina: Same.
[09:42] Maya: Thanks everyone. I'll follow up via email with calendar invites and the artifacts.
[09:48] Eric: Thanks all.
[09:50] (call ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker attribution may be off, some product or acronym names auto-corrected (e.g., "KV cache" was sometimes transcribed as "K-V cash"), and longer timestamps may be approximate.
